symptom: mendixlabs/mxcli#1515: `return formatDecimal($d, 2);` (a number where the String pattern goes) — `mxcli check` prints "Check passed!" with and without -p; mx check on 11.6.6 and 11.15.0 reports CE0117 "Error(s) in expression". A bare check also missed `formatDecimal($d, '#', 'en', 4)`
cause: checkCallExpr compared argument COUNTS only, though its comment and the E005 func-arg-type registry entry promised kinds; and it ran only in the catalog tier (TypeCheckProgram, `check -p --references`), so the no-project tier — where literals, parameters and declares already type the arguments — checked nothing
insight: Measure the mismatch CLASSES, one `return <expr>;` microflow each, with `mx check -j out.json`: the JSON names the document, so ~70 cases fit in one project copy (the text output only says 'at End event'). 11.6.6 and 11.15.0 agreed on every row. Integer and Long are interchangeable and both widen to Decimal, but Decimal into an Integer/Long parameter is CE0117 (addDays($dt, 1.5)), so 'numeric widening only' is the rule, not 'any number'. Turning the type check on surfaced four funcTable arities that were already false E006s on the -p tier (find/findLast take a start index, max/min are variadic and take DateTimes, dateTime takes 1-6 parts, formatDateTime's format is optional) and one that was too lenient (formatDecimal's format is required) — measure the table's arities before widening where it runs. inferKind types every [%Token%] as String; [%CurrentDateTime%] and the BeginOf/EndOf tokens are DateTimes, so the argument check types them itself. The one new diagnostic over mdl-examples was a true positive: addDays('[%CurrentDateTime%]', 7) passes a quoted string, CE0117 on both versions.
